source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} called{H7121} his twelve{H8147} disciples{H8527} and gave{H5414} them power{H3201} over every{H3605} spirit{H7307} of uncleanness{H2932}, to cast it out{H3318} from man{H120}, and to heal{H7495} every sickness{H2483} and every plague{H5061}.

one_way_hebrew: רוח טומאה — 'spirit of uncleanness': Zech 13:2's exact phrase (ואת רוח הטמאה אעביר מן הארץ, 'I will cause the unclean spirit to pass out of the land') — the one place Scripture names it. The commission enacts Zechariah's promise. And נגע (H5061) — the plague-word of Lev 13-14's leper-torah.
טומאה is the Torah's own category of ritual impurity; Greek πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων translates the halakhic term.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק מ״ג (Perek 43) begins here (the transcription's heading misprints פעק for פרק).
Howard's apparatus (10:1): מהאדם] מאדם G.

verses.translation: And these{H428} are the names{H8034} of the twelve{H8147} sent-ones{H7971}, called apostolos: Simon, called{H7121} Petros, and Andreah his brother{H251};

one_way_hebrew: השלוחים נקראו אפוסט״ולוס — the Hebrew names the office natively, שלוחים ('sent ones,' the rabbinic shaliach whose principle is 'a man's shaliach is as himself'), and then glosses it with the church's Greek word apostolos — the same Hebrew-to-foreign direction as evangeli (24:14) and ipocrates (6:2). A translator from Greek would have started from ἀπόστολοι and never glossed his own source-word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:2): the loanword אפוסטולוס is spelled variously (אפושטולוש A, אפוסטלוס B, אפוסטוליס D); פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פטרוס B, פיטרוש DG; סימון] שימון ABDG; EF omit נקראו... אחיו. The British Library ms carries a marginal gloss in Romance transliteration (יקופוס די זיבידיאו... 'Jacopo di Zebedeo... Giovanni'), naming the apostles in the vernacular.

verses.translation: Philippos and Bortolameos; Jacob{H3290}, called Gaimi, and Yochanan{H3110} his brother{H251}, sons{H1121} of Zavdiel; Tomas; and Mattityah{H4993}, that is Matyeo, who lent{H3867} at interest publicly; and Jacob{H3290} of Alufei, and Tereos;

greek_deviations: ומתתיה הוא מאט״יאו מלוה בריבית בפרסום — 'Mattityah, that is Matyeo, who lent at interest PUBLICLY': the Hebrew list identifies Matthew not as τελώνης ('tax collector') but as a notorious moneylender — matching his post at 'the table of exchange' (9:9). No Greek text carries this; it is the Hebrew tradition's own memory of the man at the shulchan.
translation_notes: יעקב נקרא גאי״מי — Jacob 'called Gaimi': the Spanish Jaime, glossing the apostle's name in the reader's vernacular; זבדיאל for Zebedee; וטריא״וס — the base spelling for Thaddeus (mss read וטדיאוש and the like, with ד for the base's ר).
ריבית — the rabbinic word for interest (Torah: נשך/תרבית, Lev 25:36); no biblical Strong's for this form.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:3): ובורטולאמיאוס] ובירטולומיאוש A (and similar spellings in the other mss); טומאס] טומאש AEG; זבדיאל] זבדאל DEF; וטריאוס] וטדיאוש A (and similar); בריבית] ברבית DEFG; גאימי] גיאימי EF.

verses.translation: Shimon{H8095} the Kenaani{H3669} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Simon Kananaios — and Yudah{H3063} Iscariota, who after{H310} this{H2088} betrayed him{H4560}.

one_way_hebrew: שמעון כנעני glossed 'Simon Kananaios' — the Greek Κananαῖος is itself a transliteration of the Hebrew קנאי/כנעני; the Hebrew text has the word the Greek borrowed, then adds the foreign form as a gloss for readers who knew it.
מסרהו (H4560) — 'handed him over': the Hebrew verb behind παραδίδωμι, the mesirah of a man to his captors.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:4): קאנאנאיוס] קנאניוש A, קאנאניוס BCD; ויודא] ויהודה A, וידא EF; אסקאריוטה] spelled variously (אישקריוטו A, איסכוריוטו B, אסכריוטא C, איסקריוטא EF); זה] omit B; מסרהו] מסרוהו B.

verses.translation: These{H428} twelve{H8147}{H6240} Yeshua{H3442} sent{H7971}, and commanded{H6680} them, saying{H559}: Into the lands{H776} of the nations{H1471} do not go{H1980}, and into the cities{H5892} of the Samaritans{H8118} do not enter{H935};

textual_notes: The circulating transcription read על תלכו; the scan reads אל תלכו — corrected.

verses.translation: go{H1980} to the sheep{H6629} that were driven out{H5080} from the house{H1004} of Israel{H3478},

one_way_hebrew: נדחו (H5080) — 'DRIVEN OUT, banished': the regathering word of the prophets — 'I will assemble her that was driven out (והנדחה אקבצה),' Mic 4:6; Zeph 3:19; Deut 30:4 (נדחך, 'thine outcasts'). Greek has ἀπολωλότα ('lost'); the Hebrew says the sheep were pushed out — and the mission is Deut 30:4's ingathering begun. Jer 50:6 joins both pictures: 'My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray.'

verses.translation: and herald{H1319} to them that the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is about to be established{H6965}.

greek_deviations: 'Herald that the kingdom of heaven WILL BE ESTABLISHED (שתתקיים)' — where Greek reads ἤγγικεν ('is at hand'). The base text announces the kingdom's firm establishment (קום, the verb of Dan 2:44 — 'the God of heaven shall SET UP a kingdom which shall never be destroyed'); mss ABDEFG read שתתקרב ('draws near'), assimilating to the Greek. The Hebrew's promise is Daniel's.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:7): שתתקיים] שתתקרב ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Heal{H7495} the sick{H2470}, bring the dead{H4191} to life{H2421}, cleanse{H2891} the lepers{H6879}, and cast out{H3318} the demons{H7700} from the sons{H1121} of man{H120}. And take{H6901} no reward{H7939}: freely{H2600} you received{H6901}, and freely give{H5414}.

one_way_hebrew: חנם קבלתם ובחנם תתנו — the חנם of Num 11:5 and of Torah-teaching ethics (m. Avot 1:13; b. Bek. 29a — 'as I taught you for nothing, so teach for nothing,' derived from Deut 4:5): the mission rule is the rabbinic rule of unpaid Torah.
translation_notes: והנה טהרתם — the printed text is rough ('and behold you cleansed'); mss ABDEFG read וטהרו ('and cleanse'), the plain imperative the sequence requires.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:8): והנה טהרתם] וטהרו ABDEFG; החולים] חולים A; המתים] מתים A; תקבלו] תקבל G.

verses.translation: Do not heap up{H6651} silver{H3701} and gold{H2091}, nor mammon in your purses{H3599};

one_way_hebrew: כיס (H3599) — the purse of Prov 1:14 ('let us all have one purse') and the deceitful weights kept בכיס (Deut 25:13); and ממון — the Hebrew text uses mammon HERE, where Greek 6:24 used it and the Hebrew there had 'the world': the word is native property-Hebrew (m. Avot 2:12), not a foreign import.
תצברו (H6651) — the same hoarding verb as 6:19 (Job 27:16): the missionaries are put under the treasure-teaching they carry.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:9): בכיסכם] בכסכים A.

verses.translation: nor changes{H2487} of raiment{H8071}, nor shoes{H4515}, nor a staff{H4731} in your hand{H3027}. The worker{H6466} is worthy to receive{H6901} enough{H1767} for his food{H396}.

one_way_hebrew: חליפות שמלות — 'changes of raiment,' Joseph's exact gift-phrase (חלפות שמלת, Gen 45:22; Judg 14:12): the Hebrew idiom for a spare wardrobe. Greek 'two coats' (δύο χιτῶνας) counts garments; the Hebrew names the institution.
די אכילתו — 'enough for his eating': the worker's claim measured by the ox of Deut 25:4 and the day-laborer of Deut 24:15; Greek 'his food' (τῆς τροφῆς) without the די of sufficiency.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription read ילא מקל; the scan reads ולא מקל — corrected.
Howard's apparatus (10:10): לקבל] לקבלהו DG; די] omit DEFG.

verses.translation: And in every city{H5892} and in every tower{H4026} that you enter{H935}, ask who{H4310} is the good{H2896} man{H376} among them{H8432}, and there{H8033} rest{H5117} until{H5704} you leave{H3318}.

one_way_hebrew: תנוחו — 'there REST': the mission lodges in מנוחה, the rest-word of Ruth 1:9 and Ps 23:2; Greek μείνατε ('remain') is neutral lodging.
greek_deviations: 'City and TOWER (מגדל)' again for Greek 'city and village' (cf. 9:35) — the Hebrew-family reading shared with the Vat. Ebr. 100 text.
translation_notes: The base text is elliptical — 'who is the good man among them' — with the verb of asking left unexpressed; mss ABDEF supply שאלו את ('ask'). Howard: '(ask) who is the good man.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:11): תבואו] + שאלו את ABDEF, + שאלו G; ושם] omit G.

verses.translation: And when you enter{H935} the house{H1004}, give{H5414} them shalom{H7965}, saying{H559}: Shalom{H7965} to this{H2063} house{H1004}; shalom to all{H3605} who dwell{H3427} within it{H8432}.

one_way_hebrew: The Hebrew spells the greeting out — שלום בזאת הבית שלום לכל היושבים בתוכה — the blessing David sent to Nabal's house: 'Shalom to thee, and shalom to thine house, and shalom unto all that thou hast' (1 Sam 25:6). Greek 'salute it' (ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν) hides the liturgy the Hebrew preserves; the shalom given, returning, and resting (v. 13) is a Hebrew blessing-economy.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:12): להם] לה ABDEFG ('give IT [the house] shalom').

verses.translation: And if that house{H1004} should be worthy, your shalom{H7965} will come{H935} upon it; but if it is not worthy, your shalom will return{H7725} to you.

one_way_hebrew: תשוב שלומכם — the blessing that returns to its sender: Ps 35:13, ותפלתי על חיקי תשוב ('my prayer returned into mine own bosom'). Blessing is substance in Hebrew thought; it goes, rests, or comes back.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:13): ואם²] וא״ל G; ההיא] omit A.

verses.translation: And whoever does not receive{H6901} you, and whoever does not listen{H8085} to you — go out{H3318} from that house{H1004} and remove{H6275} your feet{H7272} from the dust{H6083}.

greek_deviations: 'REMOVE your feet from the dust' (והעתקם, the removal-verb of Gen 12:8, ויעתק משם) — the base text lifts the feet out of the place's dust, where the Greek shakes the place's dust off the feet (ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτόν). Mss ABDEF read ותערו and G ונערו ('shake off'), assimilating to the Greek picture.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:14): אתכם] אליכם ABDEFG; תצאו] + חוצה A; מן הבית ההיא] מן העיר או מהבית ההיא G; והעתקם] ותערו ABDEF, ונערו G; מן העפר] מהעפר ADEF.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I speak{H1696} to you: it will be more{H3148} tolerable{H2896} for Sodom{H5467} and Gomorrah{H6017} in that day{H3117} than for that city{H5892}.

one_way_hebrew: ביום ההוא — 'IN THAT DAY,' the prophets' fixed formula for the day of judgment (Isa 2:11,17; Zech 14 throughout); Greek 'in the day of judgment' (ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως) spells out what the Hebrew idiom already carries.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:15): G reorders ביום ההוא מן העיר ההיא; אליכם] לכם AG.

verses.translation: Behold{H2009}, I am sending{H7971} you like sheep{H6629} among{H996} the wolves{H2061}: be crafty{H6175} as serpents{H5175} and lowly{H6041} as doves{H3123}.

one_way_hebrew: ערומים כנחשים — Gen 3:1's own pun: והנחש היה ערום ('the serpent was more CRAFTY') — the pair ערום/נחש is Genesis' wordplay, reused whole. Greek φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις translates the sense and loses the Eden echo.

ועניים כיונים — 'LOWLY as doves': עני (H6041), the Psalter's afflicted-humble one, with the moaning dove of Isa 38:14; 59:11. Greek ἀκέραιοι ('unmixed, innocent') is a purity word; the Hebrew is a poverty-of-spirit word. Mss ABDEFG read וענוים ('meek') — the same root either way, against the Greek.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק מ״ד (Perek 44) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (10:16): בין] בקרב ABDEFG; כצאן] כמו הצאן ABDEFG; ועניים] וענוים ABDEFG; אתכם] לכם EF; הנני] הנה EF; הזאבים] זאבים A.

verses.translation: Beware{H2094} of the sons{H1121} of man{H120}: they will hand you over{H4560} not in their assemblies{H6952} and their houses{H1004} of assembly{H3664},

greek_deviations: Read with v. 18 (as Howard construes): 'they will deliver you up NOT in their assemblies and synagogues, BUT to governors and kings.' In Greek Matthew the synagogues are where the flogging happens (εἰς συνέδρια... ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν); in the Hebrew base text the handing-over bypasses the community's own courts and goes to the civil power. Ms A reads שלא ('lest they deliver you'), easing toward the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:17): לא] שלא A; בקהלותם] בקהילותם G.

verses.translation: but to governors{H6346} and to kings{H4428}. You will be able{H3201} for my sake{H1157} to testify{H5749} to them and to the nations{H1471}.

one_way_hebrew: פחות (H6346) — the governors of the Persian chancery (Neh 2:7,9; Hag 1:1): the Hebrew uses the Bible's own word for imperial officialdom. And להעיד (H5749) — the covenant verb of calling witness (Deut 30:19); the arrest becomes a testimony-stand.
תוכלון — the archaic paragogic form (as Deut 12:17 לא תוכל), a native biblicism no back-translator produces.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:18): תוכלון] תוכלו EG; ולמלכים] ולמלאכים C; EF transpose ולפחות ולמלכים.

verses.translation: When they seize{H8610} you, do not consider{H2803} what you will say{H559}, for in the hour{H8160} that you need{H6878} it, an answer{H4617} will come{H935} to you.

one_way_hebrew: מענה (H4617) — Prov 16:1: 'The preparations of the heart in man, and the ANSWER OF THE TONGUE (מענה לשון), is from YHWH.' The promise is Proverbs' sentence turned into a mission-word: stop preparing the heart's case; the ma'aneh comes from God. Greek ('it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak') states the gift; the Hebrew names Proverbs' word for it.
translation_notes: The printed base reads אם תחשבו ('if you consider'); mss ABDEFG read אל ('do NOT consider'), which Howard follows and the sense requires.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:19): אם] אל ABDEFG; יתפשו] תתפשו G; שתצטרכו] שתצרכו AG.

verses.translation: It is not{H369} you who speak{H1696}, but the holy{H6944} spirit{H7307} of my Father{H1} — it is that which speaks{H1696} in you.

one_way_hebrew: רוח קדשו — 'HIS HOLY SPIRIT': the exact form of Isa 63:10-11 (את רוח קדשו), the only place Scripture says it — 'they rebelled, and vexed his holy spirit... where is he that put his holy spirit within him?' The Hebrew Matthew answers Isaiah's 'where?': speaking in the seized disciples. Greek 'the Spirit of your Father' loses the Isaian form.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:20): קדשו] הקדש EF; המדברים] מדברים EFG.

verses.translation: Brother{H251} will hand over{H4560} brother{H251} to death{H4194}, and the father{H1} his son{H1121}; and the sons{H1121} will rise up{H6965} against{H5921} the fathers{H1} and will lead{H2986} them unto death{H4194}.

one_way_hebrew: The scene is Mic 7:6 — 'the son dishonoureth the father... a man's enemies are the men of his own house' — the same text that surfaces at vv. 35-36. ויובילו (H2986) — 'led' as a sheep is led (Isa 53:7, כשה לטבח יובל): the family leads its own to death in the Servant's verb.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:21): האבות] אבותם ABDEFG; ויקומו] יקומו G.

verses.translation: And you will be a derision{H3933} and a horror{H2189} to all{H3605} the peoples{H5971} because of my name{H8034}; yet surely{H403} whoever{H4310} bears{H5445} it until the time{H6256} of the end{H7093} will be saved{H3467}.

one_way_hebrew: לעג וזעוה — the covenant-curse pair: לעג is the derision of Ps 44:14 ('a scorn and derision to them round about us'), זעוה (H2189) is Deut 28:25's curse-word ('thou shalt be a horror unto all the kingdoms of the earth') and Jer 29:18. Greek 'ye shall be hated' flattens two curse-terms into one emotion.
עד עת קץ — 'until the TIME OF THE END': Daniel's sealed phrase, עת קץ (Dan 11:35; 12:4,9). Greek εἰς τέλος ('to the end') is generic; the Hebrew dates the endurance to Daniel's horizon.

שיסבול — 'whoever BEARS it': the Servant's carrying-verb (סבל, Isa 53:4,11 — יסבל), the same word the text quoted at 8:17. Whoever carries as the Servant carried, to Daniel's end, will be saved (יושע — the root of ישו״ע again, as at 24:13).
textual_notes: The circulating transcription read שכן; the scan reads אכן — corrected.
Howard's apparatus (10:22): שמי] omit G.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: When they pursue{H7291} you in this{H2063} city{H5892}, flee{H1272} to another{H312}. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, you will not complete{H7999} for yourselves the cities{H5892} of Israel{H3478} before the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} comes{H935}.

textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק מ״ה (Perek 45) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (10:23): לכם²] לסבוב ABDEFG ('to traverse,' toward the Greek τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις); כי] omit ABDEF; האדם] אדם ABDEF; ברחו] + לכם G.

verses.translation: No{H369} disciple{H8527} is greater{H1419} than his rav, nor the servant{H5650} greater than his master{H113}.

translation_notes: רב — the rabbinic title again (cf. 9:11); the saying is a beit-midrash proverb in its native dress.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:24): תלמיד] התלמיד ABDEFG.

verses.translation: It is enough{H1767} for the disciple{H8527} to be as his rav, and the servant{H5650} as his master{H113}. If they call{H7121} the master{H1167} of the house{H1004} Baal Zevuv{H2070}, how much more the sons{H1121} of his house!

one_way_hebrew: בעל זבוב — the Hebrew has the actual biblical name: Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kgs 1:2-6). Greek Matthew's Βεελζεβούλ ('-zeboul') is a distorted transliteration; the Hebrew text and 2 Kings agree against it letter for letter. Only in Hebrew does the insult quote Elijah's polemic — the master of the house called by the fly-god's name.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:25): יקראו] קראו G.

verses.translation: Do not fear{H3372} them, for there is no{H369} thing{H1697} that will not be seen{H7200}, nor hidden{H5956}.

one_way_hebrew: In the unpointed text תראו ('fear') and יראה ('will be seen') share their consonantal root-shapes — fear not, for all will be seen: the assonance of ירא/ראה is Hebrew's own (cf. 9:8). And נעלם (H5956) — Qohelet's word for what God brings to light: 'God shall bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing (כל נעלם)' (Eccl 12:14) — the saying is Qohelet's verdict as comfort.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:26): נעלם] + שלא יודע ABDEF, + יודע G ('that shall not be known').

verses.translation: What I say{H559} to you in the darkness{H2822}, say it in the light{H216}.

greek_deviations: The base text is a single clause — dark to light — without the Greek's second member ('what ye hear in the ear, preach upon the housetops'). Mss ABDEFG supply a version of it: ואשר לאוזן ספרו אותו בשער ('and what [you hear] in the ear, tell it AT THE GATE') — and even the expansion says the city GATE, the Hebrew place of public speech (Ruth 4:1; Prov 31:23), not the Greek's housetops.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:27): Beginning] + אשר ABDEFG; ABDEFG add (with variations) ואשר לאוזן ספרו אותו בשער; DG add ואשר תשמעו.

verses.translation: And do not be afraid{H6342} of those who kill{H2026}, who have no power in their hand{H3027} to kill{H2026} the souls{H5315}; but fear{H6342} the one who has power{H3201} in his hand{H3027} to destroy{H6} the soul{H5315} and the body{H1480} in Gehinnom.

one_way_hebrew: The Hebrew turns on יד — 'in whose HAND' the power lies (אין בידם... יכולת בידו): Job 12:10's confession, 'in whose hand is the soul of every living thing.' Greek δυναμένων/δυνάμενον keeps the ability and loses the hand.
translation_notes: מהורגי — the construct stands bare ('the killers of—'); mss BEF supply הגויות and DG הגוף ('killers of the BODY'), completing the expected antithesis. Howard: 'those who kill (bodies).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:28): מהורגי] + הגויות BEF, + הגוף DG, + הגוות A; והגוף] וגוף F; בגהינם] בגיהנם BDG.

verses.translation: Do not two{H8147} sparrows{H6833} perish{H6} for one{H259} perutah? Yet not one of them will fall{H5307} on the earth{H776} except by the will{H7522} of your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: פרוטה — the rabbinic smallest coin (the Mishnah's שוה פרוטה, the least value at law): the price is quoted in the currency of the Jewish courts. Greek ἀσσαρίου gives a Roman coin; the Hebrew gives the halakhic one.
ברצון אביכם — 'by the WILL of your Father': the sparrow falls within רצון (cf. 7:21; 8:27); Greek 'without your Father' (ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν) leaves the word unsaid.
greek_deviations: The base text reads 'two sparrows PERISH (אבדו) for a perutah' — the bargain is their death, not their sale; mss ABDEFG read ימכרו ('are sold'), as in the Greek. Howard prints '(sold).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:29): אבדו] ימכרו ABDEFG; ולא] לא G; על הארץ] לארץ EF; ברצון] + האל ית׳ EF.

verses.translation: Are not the hairs{H8185} of your heads{H7218} all{H3605} numbered{H5608}?

one_way_hebrew: שערות... ספורים — the idiom of 1 Sam 14:45 and 2 Sam 14:11: 'there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground' — the oath-formula of a life preserved to the hair; here the hairs are not only kept but COUNTED (ספר, the census-verb of Ps 147:4, 'he telleth the number of the stars').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:30): שערות] שער E; ראשיכם] ראשכם A.

verses.translation: Do not fear{H3372}, for you are better{H2896} than the sparrows{H6833}.

translation_notes: The printed base ends אדם ('man is better than sparrows'); mss BCDEFG read אתם ('YOU are better'), which the address requires — a ד/ת slip in the base. Howard: '(you) are better than the sparrows.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:31): אדם] אתם BCDEFG; מצפורים] מציפרים A.

verses.translation: Whoever praises{H7623} me before{H6440} man{H120}, I will praise him{H7623} before{H6440} my Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

greek_deviations: המשבח — 'whoever PRAISES me... I will praise him': the Hebrew runs on שבח (the praise-verb of Ps 63:4; 117:1), mutual praise between the disciple and his Lord, where Greek has ὁμολογήσει ('confess/acknowledge'). Confession is a courtroom word; שבח is a doxology word — the Hebrew disciple praises, and is praised.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription read אשבחבנו; the scan reads אשבחנו — corrected.
Howard's apparatus (10:32): לפני] + בני C(?); בפני] לפני A.

GREEK 10:33 ('but whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father') HAS NO COUNTERPART IN THE SHEM TOV TEXT: Howard's apparatus states, 'All mss omit vs 33 except A which reads: ואשר יכחש בי לפני בני אדם אכחש בו לפני אבי שבשמים.' The text runs directly from v. 32 to v. 34; only the late ms A supplies the denial-clause, assimilating to the Greek. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries a form of the verse ('he who treats me as a stranger... I will cause him to perish before El my Father').

verses.translation: In that hour{H8160} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Do not think{H2803} that I have come{H935} to put{H7760} anything in the earth{H776} but a sword{H2719}.

translation_notes: The base text lacks שלום ('peace'): it reads 'that I came to put in the earth — except a sword,' coherent as it stands ('to put nothing in the earth but a sword'); mss ABD add שלום and EFG read לשום שלום, as in the Greek. Howard: 'to put (peace) on the earth, but a sword.'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק מ״ו (Perek 46) begins here (following v. 32, since the text lacks v. 33).
The circulating transcription read על תחשבו; the scan reads אל תחשבו — corrected.
Howard's apparatus (10:34): לשים] + שלום ABD, לשום שלום EFG.

verses.translation: I have come{H935} to separate{H6504} mankind{H120}: the son{H1121} from his father{H1}, and the daughter{H1323} from her mother{H517}.

one_way_hebrew: The text under this saying is Mic 7:6 — 'son dishonoureth father, daughter riseth up against her mother' — and the Hebrew keeps Micah's two pairs; Greek Matthew adds the daughter-in-law/mother-in-law third pair from the same Micah verse. להפריד (H6504) — the separating of Gen 13:9,14 (Abram and Lot): kinship sundered for the covenant's sake.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:35): (no significant variants recorded).

verses.translation: And enemies{H341} will be those once beloved{H157}.

greek_deviations: Greek 10:36 reads 'a man's foes shall be they of his own household' (Mic 7:6's אנשי ביתו); the Hebrew compresses it to a proverb of three words — האויבים להיות אהובים, 'the enemies will be the beloved' — enmity springing from love itself. Mss ABDEFG read אוהבים ('those who love him'); the Vat. Ebr. 100 text has 'acquainted ones against their acquaintances.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:36): אהובים] אוהבים ABDEFG; להיות] שהיו DG.

verses.translation: He who loves{H157} his father{H1} and his mother{H517} more{H3148} than me — I am not suited for him.

greek_deviations: The base text reads איני ראוי לו — 'I am not suited for HIM' — the reverse of the Greek's 'he is not worthy of me' (which mss AD restore, אינו ראוי לי). Howard translates the base as it stands: 'I am not suitable for him.' Read plainly, the saying disqualifies not the man before the master but the master's fitness FOR that man: to one who loves father and mother more, this teacher is of no use.
The Greek's second clause ('he that loveth son or daughter more than me...') is absent.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:37): איני ראוי לו] אינו ראוי לי AD.

GREEK 10:38 ('and he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me') HAS NO COUNTERPART IN THE SHEM TOV TEXT: Howard's apparatus states, 'All mss omit vs 38.' The text runs directly from v. 37 to v. 39. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise passes from v. 37 to v. 39 — both independent Hebrew Matthew traditions lack the cross-saying here.

verses.translation: He who loves{H157} his soul{H5315} will lose it{H6}; he who loses{H6} it for my sake will find it{H4672}.

translation_notes: The printed base reads האובד אותי ('he who loses ME'); mss AEF read אותה ('it'), which the parallel requires and Howard follows ('he who loses (it) for my sake'). בשבילי — rabbinic Hebrew 'for my sake.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:39): אותי] אותה AEF; יאבדיה] יאבדנה ABDEFG; בשבילי ימצאנה] omit G.

verses.translation: He who receives{H6901} you receives me; and he who receives me receives him who sent me{H7971}.

one_way_hebrew: The saying is the rabbinic law of the שליח (cf. v. 2): שלוחו של אדם כמותו — 'a man's sent-one is as himself' (m. Ber. 5:5). Receiving the shaliach is receiving the sender; the verse states the agency principle the Hebrew word שלוחים carried from the start. Greek ἀπόστολος borrowed the office; the Hebrew supplies its law.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (10:40): המקבל... אותי²] omit G (haplography).

verses.translation: He who receives{H6901} a prophet{H5030} in the name{H8034} of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward{H7939}; and he who receives a righteous man{H6662} in the name of a righteous man will receive the reward of the righteous.

one_way_hebrew: לשם — 'FOR THE NAME of': the rabbinic לשמה, doing a thing for its own name's sake (m. Avot 2:12, 'let all thy deeds be done לשם שמים — for the name of Heaven'). Greek εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου carries the Hebrew idiom bodily into Greek, where it has puzzled readers ever since; here it is at home.

The prophet and the tsaddik hosted for their name recall the Shunammite and Elisha (2 Kgs 4:8-10) and the widow and Elijah (1 Kgs 17) — the reward of the hostess was the prophet's own reward: a son, and a son raised.

verses.translation: And he who gives{H5414} one{H259} vessel{H3627} of cold{H7119} water{H4325} to one of my little{H6996} disciples{H8527}, in the name{H8034} of my disciple — amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, his reward{H7939} will not be lost{H6}.

one_way_hebrew: מים קרים — 'COLD WATER': Prov 25:25, מים קרים על נפש עיפה ('as cold waters to a weary soul, so is good news from a far country') — and the mission of this chapter is exactly good news carried far (v. 7). The least gift to the least disciple is Proverbs' verse enacted; Greek ψυχροῦ ('a cup of cold') keeps the temperature and loses the proverb.
textual_notes: The ms abbreviates: כלי א״ = כלי אחד ('one vessel').
Howard's apparatus (10:42): שלא] לא A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 10 in the Shem Tov Hebrew commissions the twelve in the Torah's own categories and lacks two Greek verses outright. (1) THE TEXT HAS NO 10:33 ('whosoever shall deny me...'): Howard's apparatus — 'All mss omit vs 33 except A,' which alone supplies it, assimilating to the Greek; the text runs from v. 32 to v. 34. (2) THE TEXT HAS NO 10:38 ('he that taketh not his cross...'): 'All mss omit vs 38' — and the independent Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise passes from v. 37 to v. 39: both Hebrew traditions lack the cross-saying. (3) 10:32 runs on PRAISE, not confession — 'whoever praises (המשבח) me before man, I will praise him'; and 10:37 reads 'he who loves his father and mother more than me — I am not suited for HIM' (mss AD reverse to the Greek's 'he is not worthy of me'). (4) 10:7: the kingdom 'is about to be ESTABLISHED (שתתקיים)' — Dan 2:44's verb — where Greek has 'is at hand' (mss assimilate to 'draws near'). (5) 10:2 names the office natively and glosses it — השלוחים 'called apostolos' — and 10:3 remembers Matthew as מתתיה 'who lent at interest publicly' (no Greek text has it); 10:25 has the real biblical name בעל זבוב (2 Kgs 1:2) against Greek 'Beelzeboul.' (6) 10:6 sends to the sheep 'that were DRIVEN OUT (נדחו)' of the house of Israel — the prophets' regathering word (Mic 4:6; Deut 30:4) — not 'lost'; 10:16 reuses Gen 3:1's own pun (ערומים כנחשים) and makes the dove 'lowly' (עניים), not 'innocent.' (7) 10:17-18 (as Howard construes): 'they will deliver you up NOT in their assemblies and synagogues, BUT to governors and kings' — the synagogues are not the flogging-place they are in the Greek. (8) 10:19-20: the answer under arrest is Prov 16:1's מענה ('the answer of the tongue is from YHWH'), spoken by 'HIS HOLY SPIRIT' (רוח קדשו — Isa 63:10-11's exact form) of my Father. (9) 10:22: 'a derision and a HORROR (זעוה, Deut 28:25) to all the peoples... whoever BEARS it (יסבול, Isa 53:4) until the TIME OF THE END (עת קץ, Dan 12:4) will be saved.' (10) 10:34 base lacks 'peace': 'do not think I came to put anything in the earth but a sword'; 10:29 base: sparrows 'PERISH for a perutah' (mss: 'are sold'); 10:12 spells out the shalom-greeting of 1 Sam 25:6; 10:42's cold water is Prov 25:25. Scan corrections to the transcription: 10:5 אל, 10:10 ולא, 10:22 אכן, 10:32 אשבחנו, 10:34 אל. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 43), 16 (44), 23 (45), and 34 (46).
